vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: macro-helper
Version: 1.0.1

The macro-helper skill is a legitimate utility designed to assist users with Excel VBA development. The core logic in scripts/macro.sh consists of static text templates and educational content for generating, debugging, and optimizing VBA code, with no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's files and runtime instructions are consistent with an Excel/VBA macro helper: it ships an informational bash script that prints VBA templates, explanations, and debugging tips and does not request credentials, perform installs, or show signs of exfiltration.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Excel macro & VBA helper) match the included assets: SKILL.md, tips.md, and a scripts/macro.sh that outputs VBA generators, explainers, templates and debug advice. Nothing required (env, binaries) is disproportionate to this purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run the included script (bash scripts/macro.sh <command> [task_description]) and to present generated/commented VBA. The script only emits text (VBA snippets, guidance) and does not instruct reading unrelated files, contacting external endpoints, or collecting system secrets.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install specification is provided (instruction-only plus a bundled script). No downloads, package installs, or archive extraction are present in the repository, so nothing new would be written to disk beyond the existing files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, credentials, or config paths. The runtime script uses only positional parameters and local shell commands (e.g., date); it does not access or reference secrets or external service tokens.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Flags show always:false and normal invocability. The skill does not request persistent system presence or attempt to modify other skills or system-wide agent settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and self-contained: it prints VBA code and advice and does not itself contact external services or request credentials. Still, before installing or running any script from an unknown source, review scripts/manifests locally. Also be cautious about the macros the skill generates: VBA macros can perform file operations, send email via Outlook, or modify system files—review and test generated macros in a safe environment and do not enable or run macros in untrusted workbooks. If you need stronger assurance, ask the publisher for a signed release or review the entire scripts/macro.sh content (it is included) before use.
